solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Poignancy, though in former times, mostly (6)

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece within another, so the short though sits within the shortened past
'mostly' means not quite all, so PAST keeps all but its final letter

blocks.note: PAST (former times) without its last letter
tho is the informal spelling of though

annotation.surface: Someone reflecting that a certain sadness belonged mostly to the old days.
annotation.walkthrough: Though looks like a link word tying the halves together; it is a piece of the wordplay in its informal spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pathos is the quality in a story or scene that stirs pity, which is what poignancy names.

entries.clue: Write note in a single sheet attachment (9)

indicators.note: 'in' places the written note within the sheet, as words go on a page

blocks.note: the article taken as it stands
a page is a single sheet of a book
to pen is to write
D is one of the musical notes

annotation.surface: An instruction to jot a note on a single sheet sent as an attachment, like an email file.
annotation.walkthrough: Attachment makes you think of a file sent with an email; the definition is an add-on or limb, and the single sheet is a book's.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an appendage is anything attached to something larger, from a limb to a supplement.

entries.clue: Captive deer trapped in weed (7)

indicators.note: something trapped in a thing is enclosed by it, so the deer goes inside the weeding word

blocks.note: to hoe is to weed a bed
a stag is a male deer

annotation.surface: A deer caught fast in a tangle of weeds, held captive.
annotation.walkthrough: Weed looks like a noun, a plant for the deer to be tangled in; it is the gardening verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Captive as a noun: a hostage is a person held by force to secure a bargain.

entries.clue: What’s leading summer each year? Spring (3)

indicators.note: what leads a word is its front, so take the first letter of summer

blocks.note: the first letter of summer
p.a., per annum, is Latin for each year

annotation.surface: A riddle about the seasons: what comes before summer every year? Spring, of course.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants spring to be the season that leads summer; it is a mineral spring.
annotation.definitionFit: Spring in its sense of a natural source of water: a spa is a mineral spring, and by extension the resort around it.

entries.clue: Count rat in a way to be this? (8)

definitions.text: Count rat in a way to be this?

indicators.note: putting letters in another way means rearranging them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A count who rats on his side is asked whether that makes him one.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a count who ratted, changing sides, would be exactly this.
annotation.definitionFit: To rat is to betray your side, and one who does so is a turncoat, so the whole clue reads straight.

entries.clue: Character in Iliad who volunteered to serve (5)

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, with its article

annotation.surface: A figure from Homer's Iliad who stepped forward to fight.
annotation.walkthrough: The Iliad makes you think of a hero such as Achilles; the character is a letter of the Greek alphabet. The TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer army, so those who volunteered are THE TA.
annotation.definitionFit: Character in its sense of a written letter: theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet the Iliad is written in.

entries.clue: Answer lies in handy loom needing no fittings (5-2-4)

indicators.note: something that lies in a place rests inside it, so the answer's A sits within the looming word

blocks.note: handy, ready to hand
to loom over is to tower
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

annotation.surface: A craft tip: the solution lies in a handy loom that needs no extra fittings.
annotation.walkthrough: Loom looks like the weaving frame, which suits the clothing answer; it is the verb, to loom or tower.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: ready-to-wear clothes come in standard sizes, so no tailor's fittings are required.

entries.clue: Blimp perhaps endlessly circling good German city (7)

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of COLONEL is dropped
to circle something is to go round it, so the shortened colonel surrounds the letter for good

blocks.note: COLONEL, as in Colonel Blimp, without its last letter
G is the usual abbreviation for good

annotation.surface: An airship endlessly circling above a German city.
annotation.walkthrough: Blimp suggests an airship; it is Colonel Blimp, a pompous old British officer from a 1930s newspaper cartoon, so Blimp is an example of a colonel.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain naming: Cologne (Köln) is a city on the Rhine in western Germany.

entries.clue: This is noble, the third exiled from ancient Spanish kingdom (5)

indicators.note: to be exiled is to be sent out, so the third letter is removed

blocks.note: Aragon was a medieval kingdom in north-east Spain
the kingdom loses its third letter, A

annotation.surface: A nobleman forced into exile from an old Spanish kingdom.
annotation.walkthrough: Noble suggests a Spanish grandee; here it is chemistry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: argon is one of the noble gases, so 'this is noble' is a chemist's way of pointing to it.

entries.clue: Renegade with an attitude about tattoo (8)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the attitude is wrapped around the tattoo

blocks.note: an is the article A
a pose is an attitude struck
tat is short for tattoo

annotation.surface: A rebel with attitude, and a tattoo to prove it.
annotation.walkthrough: The tattoo and the attitude paint a rebel, which fits the definition, but the definition is the religious sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an apostate abandons their faith or party, as a renegade does.

entries.clue: Claim everything for instance European (6)

blocks.note: all = everything
e.g., for instance
E for European

annotation.surface: Someone claiming everything, a European for example.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces simply run in the order the clue gives them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to allege is to claim something, usually without proof.

entries.clue: Is any train running in an unclean state? (10)

indicators.note: letters that are running are on the move, not staying in their printed order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A passenger asking if any train is running in a filthy condition.
annotation.walkthrough: Running looks like a train in service; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: insanitary describes a place dirty enough to be a health risk.

entries.clue: Cheeky rascal reconfigured internet (11)

indicators.note: to reconfigure is to set up in a new arrangement, so the letters of internet are reordered

blocks.note: an imp is a little rascal
anagram of INTERNET

annotation.surface: A cheeky young rascal who has reconfigured the internet.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheeky and rascal sit side by side like a single description; the rascal belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: impertinent describes a lack of respect, the same cheek a rascal shows.

entries.clue: Essential part of analysing unknown sticky substance (4)

indicators.note: the essential part of something is its core, so the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: found across the join of the two words

annotation.surface: A lab testing an unknown sticky substance.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, from the last letter of analysing into unknown.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal word: gunk is any sticky, messy substance.

entries.clue: Weak eddying causing water turbulence (4)

indicators.note: eddying water swirls round, so the letters swirl into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters

annotation.surface: Feeble eddies stirring up the water.
annotation.walkthrough: Eddying fits the watery surface so well it barely looks like an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a wake is the churned water left behind a moving boat.

entries.clue: Wonderful friend guarding female round soldiers (10)

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, so the friend surrounds the middle pieces

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
a hen is a female bird
O is round in shape
soldiers are men, as in officers and men

annotation.surface: A marvellous friend who protects a woman surrounded by soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: Round reads as surrounding, a second container signal; it is only the letter O, run on in sequence.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: phenomenal describes something extraordinary enough to wonder at.

entries.clue: Go out — be coming back holding key? (3)

indicators.note: something coming back travels the opposite way, so be is reversed
to hold is to contain, so the reversed word has the key inside it

blocks.note: the word taken as it stands
B is a musical key

annotation.surface: Leave, and then come back with the key.
annotation.walkthrough: Go out is the tide going out; the surface makes it a person leaving the house.
annotation.definitionFit: The tidal sense: water that recedes from the shore is said to ebb.

entries.clue: Muscles suffering, reportedly letting oneself down (9)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the answer only sounds like the wordplay

blocks.note: abs are stomach muscles; ailing is suffering

annotation.surface: Aching muscles letting someone down.
annotation.walkthrough: Letting oneself down reads as failing; it is lowering yourself on a rope.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of an idiom: abseiling is descending a cliff by rope, lowering your own body.

entries.clue: With some chance of restoration theatre being OK to broadcast (10)

blocks.note: rep is repertory theatre
fit to air, to put on radio or TV

annotation.surface: A Restoration theatre play just about fit to be broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: Restoration theatre suggests the English drama after 1660; the definition takes restoration as plain mending.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: whatever can be mended stands some chance of being restored.

entries.clue: Quite a hit introducing new museum piece (7)

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so quite and a are jumbled
to introduce is to bring in, so the letter for new is placed inside the jumble

blocks.note: anagram of QUITE A
N is short for new

annotation.surface: A new exhibit that has proved quite a hit with museum-goers.
annotation.walkthrough: Hit reads as a success; it is the anagram signal, striking the letters apart.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an antique is an old object of the kind museums display.

entries.clue: Son in company of soldiers is intimate and relaxed (4)

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece within another, so the son sits inside the company

blocks.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for a company
S for son

annotation.surface: A son serving with his company feels at ease.
annotation.walkthrough: Company alone would give CO; the full phrase company of soldiers points to the army's own abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cosy describes somewhere warm, snug and informal.

entries.clue: Starch fool’s put in sparkling wine (7)

indicators.note: to put something in is to insert it, so the fool goes inside the wine

blocks.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
an ass is a fool

annotation.surface: An odd recipe where starch and a fool go into fizz.
annotation.walkthrough: Fool looks like the fruit pudding, which fits a recipe; it is a silly person. The ’s stands for is.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: cassava is a tropical root grown for its starch, the source of tapioca.

entries.clue: Let It Be and Time included in sequence of songs (4)

indicators.note: to be included in is to be taken inside, so time goes inside the set

blocks.note: a band's set is its sequence of songs
T for time

annotation.surface: A band's setlist featuring the Beatles' Let It Be and a song called Time.
annotation.walkthrough: Let It Be is dressed as the Beatles song; it is a proofreader's instruction, Latin for let it stand.
annotation.definitionFit: A proofreading term: stet, written in a margin, tells the printer to let a deleted word be.

entries.clue: Author with a popular following beginning to tire (5)

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so with, a and popular come after the first letter of tire
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of tire
W is short for with
the article as it stands
in = popular, fashionable

annotation.surface: A popular writer whose readers are starting to lose interest.
annotation.walkthrough: A popular following looks like a writer's fan base; following is the order instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Mark Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn.

entries.clue: Trainee’s job in winter stripped navy vessel (10)

indicators.note: a stripped word has its outer layer removed, so winter loses both end letters

blocks.note: WINTER without its first and last letters
RN, the Royal Navy
a ship is a vessel

annotation.surface: A trainee sailor's winter job aboard a stripped-down naval vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: Navy and vessel make a naval picture, but the answer is office work experience.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an internship is the post an intern, a trainee, holds.

entries.clue: Teacher’s to show disapproval over unclothed form (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means above, so the tut is placed on top
unclothed means bare, stripped of its outer layer, so form loses its end letters

blocks.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
FORM without its outer letters

annotation.surface: A teacher tutting at a nude figure in life drawing class.
annotation.walkthrough: Form suggests the human body; it only supplies letters. The ’s stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tutor is a teacher, especially one who teaches individuals or small groups.

entries.clue: Brand horse queen’s breaking in (6)

indicators.note: to break in is to force entry, so the queen gets inside the horse

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse
QU is a standard abbreviation for queen

annotation.surface: Branding a horse while the queen is breaking it in.
annotation.walkthrough: Brand and breaking in paint a ranch; brand is the product name, and breaking in is the insertion signal. The ’s stands for is.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the car world: a marque is a manufacturer's make, its brand name.

entries.clue: Mistake in recording tailless reptile (8)

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece within another, so the mistake sits inside the shortened recording
without a tail, so the last letter of TAPING goes

blocks.note: TAPING (recording) without its last letter
to err is to make a mistake

annotation.surface: A slip-up while recording a reptile that has lost its tail.
annotation.walkthrough: Tailless seems to describe the reptile, as lizards shed tails; it acts on the recording.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, one kind of reptile.

entries.clue: Capital not all needed for equipment (3)

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
the city without its last letter

annotation.surface: Not all of the money needed to buy equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital reads as money; it is a capital city.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig or a sound rig.

entries.clue: Developer of fashionable IOW resort, name forgotten (8)

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so the N for name drops from the resort

blocks.note: in = fashionable
VENTNOR, a resort on the Isle of Wight (IOW, off England's south coast), without one N for name

annotation.surface: A property developer who built a smart Isle of Wight resort, now forgotten.
annotation.walkthrough: Developer suggests property; it means someone who develops new things.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an inventor develops new devices and processes.

entries.clue: Called to enter grand English country house (6)

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the calling word goes between grand and English

blocks.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
rang = called on the phone
E for English

annotation.surface: Invited to visit a grand English country house.
annotation.walkthrough: Grand looks like an adjective for the house; it is a thousand.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a grange is a country house, originally one with farm buildings attached.
